summary: Eduard Müller-Hess was an Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist. He completed his Inauguraldissertation at the University of Leipzig in 1874 and served as a professor at the University of Bern (attested 1897-1898).

Eduard Röer worked in Indology and philosophy. He studied at Jena, Königsberg under Johann Friedrich Herbart (~1827-1832), and under Franz Bopp (~1837-1839). He held posts at the East India Company (~1839-1861) and The Asiatic Society.

Eduard Sachau worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies and linguistics. He studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Halle under Nöldeke, Brockhaus, and Fleischer. He served as professor at Vienna, Frederick William University Berlin, and director of Seminar für Orientalische Sprachen.

Eduard Schwyzer was a scholar in linguistics and Indology. He held academic posts at the University of Zurich (~1912-1927), the University of Bonn (~1927-1932), and Humboldt University of Berlin (~1932-1943).

Eduard Sievers was a linguist who studied at Leipzig and Berlin under Curtius, Leskien, and Zarncke. He held professorships at the University of Jena (1871-1883), University of Tübingen (1883-1887), University of Halle (1887-1892), and University of Leipzig (1892-1922).

Eduardo Francisco Freyre Roach is a Buddhist studies scholar. He completed a Master of Buddhist Studies at the University of Hong Kong (attested 2014) under the supervision of Yakupitiyage Karunadasa and Georgios T. Halkias.

Edvard Westermarck worked in philosophy. He studied at the University of Helsinki (~1881-1889) and held academic posts at the London School of Economics (~1904-1930) and Åbo Akademi University (~1918-1932).
Edward Albert Gait was an Indologist and historian who studied at University College London. He founded the Bihar Research Society in 1914 and served as its president from 1915 to 1920.

Edward Backhouse Eastwick worked in Indology, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and linguistics. He studied at Charterhouse School, Merton College, and the University of Oxford, later holding posts at East India Company College (1845) and the Foreign Office.
Edward Burnett Tylor worked in religious studies. He studied at Grove House School and held academic posts at the University of Seville and the University of Oxford (~1883-1909).

Edward Byles Cowell worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at Oxford under Horace Hayman Wilson. Cowell held posts at Sanskrit College, Presidency University, and served as professor at Cambridge (1867-1903).

Edward C. Dimock Jr. worked in Indology and religious studies. He studied at Yale and earned his Ph.D. from Harvard Divinity School (~1953-1959). He held posts at the University of Chicago (1966-1993) and the American Institute of Indian Studies.

Edward Capps was a historian and archaeologist. He studied at Illinois College, Yale University, Berlin, Munich, and Halle. He held academic posts at Illinois College (1887-1888), Yale University (1890-1907), and Princeton University (1907-1936).
Edward Clive Bayley was an Indologist and historian. He studied at Haileybury and Imperial Service College and East India Company College (~1840-1842), entering the Indian Civil Service in 1842.

Edward Conze was a Buddhist studies and Indology scholar. He studied at Tübingen, Heidelberg, Kiel, Hamburg, Cologne (Ph.D.), and Bonn. He held posts at the University of London, University of California, Berkeley, and served as Buddhist Society Vice-President.

Edward Delavan Perry was a scholar in Indology and linguistics. He studied at Columbia University (~1871-1875) and the University of Tübingen (~1877-1879), and served as Jay Professor at Columbia University from 1891 to 1931.

Edward Denison Ross worked in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Tibetology. He studied at UCL and Strasbourg under Theodor Nöldeke. He held posts at UCL, Aliah University, the British Museum, and SOAS University of London (1916-1937).

Edward Elbridge Salisbury was a linguist and Indologist. He studied at Yale and under Silvestre de Sacy, Garcin de Tassy, Bopp, Burnouf, and Lassen. He was a professor at Yale (1841-1854) and president of the American Oriental Society.

Edward Evan Evans-Pritchard worked in religious studies. He studied at Exeter College, the University of Oxford, and the London School of Economics. He held academic posts at LSE, Cairo University, Cambridge, and Oxford (1946-1970).

Edward Fitzpatrick Crangle is a scholar in Buddhist studies, religious studies, and Indology. He completed doctoral studies under Roderick S. Bucknell (attested 1994) and held a post at the University of Sydney.
